new_possibilities: Structure shown, not told: a station-to-script table and the Solid station's node tree make the pairing (C9) and the parenting (C76, C77) readable at a glance. Neither the original nor L1 shows either.
A variable / class / role table for solid.gd, so the three new classes can be read as a set.
A hinge sentence before 1.5: 'In solid.gd the mesh and the shape agree only because the script gives them the same radius. Now you pull them apart.' It says C82 as the reason the experiment exists.
The warning correction belongs in both versions: point_position is unused at 1.12 as well; the warning names a condition that the edit only makes obvious.
Splitting 1.5 into two named tries, 'a shape larger than the mesh' and 'a shape smaller than the mesh', makes the symmetry of the two disagreements visible.

Tying the light into the thread: a light changes what is seen, not what is touched. That makes a fourth layer (lit) beside position, seen and touched, where the original only says 'Remove the light, keep the body'.
One stated sentence on why the order runs nothing, then seen, then touched. The reader needed it, and neither version says it.

The [guess] marks as an instrument: each marks a place where the compressed text is underdetermined, a diff map for the next version. Most of the 20 stuck points are terms used before they are declared, so a mechanical check (a term used before its 'gives:' line is a type error, and the declarations must be visible, not HTML comments) could catch them before a reader does.
The unfolding names the unit (metres), which CONSTRUCTION.md confirms. It could be stated, since 'the sphere rises' already depends on it.
lost_vectors: DIRECTION, the headings: the original's sections are acts the student does: 'Give the position a surface', 'Give the body a boundary', 'Remove the light, keep the body'. L1's are definitions: 'A mesh is seen', 'A shape is touched', 'A point has no body'. The thought turns from making to classifying. The title's arc, 'give the point a body', becomes a taxonomy of mesh, shape and body. The unfolding inherited the taxonomy and then had to rebuild the 'why this order' as a marked guess.

DIRECTION, the voice: the original's 'we' ('We will keep those', 'We have chosen whether the surface we see and the boundary we encounter coincide') became 'you'. The author no longer walks beside the learner. 'We have chosen' is an act already done, by editing one line, and the original places it right after that edit. 'You choose whether they agree' is a standing capacity, placed at the end of the section.

THE WORDS THAT CARRIED THE SYSTEM: 'the surface we see and the boundary we encounter' became 'seen and touched', mesh and shape. 'Encounter' tied the boundary to the museum visitor meeting the work, and it comes back in the last paragraph ('another way to change the encounter'). 'Touched' narrows that to contact. Neither 'surface' nor 'boundary' occurs in L1, so the lesson's ending and its experiments no longer share words.

FORCE, softened or changed: 'how much the sphere hides' became 'what the sphere hides' (amount became content; the reader stalled). 'A visible surface has still given it nothing to collide with' lost 'still'. 'Return both to the matching 0.14' lost 'matching', which was the reason to restore. 'without adding another required exercise' became 'adds no exercise'. 'participates in collision' became 'a body that stops things': a relation became an agent.

CAUSE INVERTED: 'The editor's unused-variable warning describes that condition' names a state that was there all along. L1's order ('Change... Nothing appears. The editor warns: unused variable. A value changed, and nothing uses it.') makes the edit the cause. The reader caught this and repaired it, so here the unfolder recovered more than the compression carried, by reasoning against it.

SHORTCUT TO SYSTEM, the feeler: 'Its movement is borrowed equipment, like the camera' became 'It is supplied, like the camera'. 'Borrowed' is a course-wide category, but in L1 it survives only in an HTML comment ('borrows:'), which is invisible when rendered. 'The fixed-camera study supplies another moving body so we can test the same relation' became 'The study's feeler moves in your place'. That dropped the reason (the camera is fixed, so you cannot walk here) and the purpose (testing the same relation), and the feeler became your proxy rather than a second body. The reader had to guess the reason.

SHORTCUT TO SYSTEM, the label: 'the contact label reports stopped' became 'does its label report stopped'. What that label is (a contact report made by contact_probe.gd, not the 'Point one' label) went ambiguous, and the unfolding confidently gave 'stopped' to the station's label. Of the two distortions after unfolding, this is the only factual one.

ACTIONS BECAME CAPTIONS: 'Open position.gd', 'Open visible.gd' and 'Open solid.gd' became 'This is X.gd' after each code block. The unfolding kept the caption form, so after compression no text tells the student to open the files. 'Its complete construction runs in the same familiar function' was dropped too, which loosens the thread from the opening 'use that moment' to each construction.

SMALL IDENTIFICATIONS: 'Restore the height' became 'Restore it', so the reader had to guess that 1.12 is the height. 'Knowing its construction gives us another way to change the encounter' lost 'another', a second way beside walking, and the reader took it as a promise to edit the museum sphere. 'keeps the roles of the supplied parts available' lost 'available'.

DECLARATIONS THAT DO NOT REACH THE READER: the type-safety apparatus (needs/gives/borrows per section, then the Types and Supplied box) is where L1 tries to make each shortcut enter its system. But the per-section declarations are HTML comments and the box comes last. So 'feeler' is used from the 1.1 title and defined only at the end, and 'museum', 'label', 'dim fill' and 'directional light' are never declared. L1 is type-safe in its source, not on the rendered page.
readability: Easy at the level of steps and code: the reader answered 14 of 16 questions correctly and surely (15/16 by the key), so the code and step layer passed almost losslessly. Hard at the connective layer: 20 stuck points, nearly all terms used before they are declared (feeler, label, museum, 'body' for both a visible node and a physics body), plus two ambiguous restores, one misleading cause, and declarations kept in HTML comments or a closing box the reader meets last.
